Same X-Cache / 404 / error semantics
Koa ki native async error flow
disadvantages: Naya framework = naya test matrix
Koa ka apna body handling bypass kiya (string body)
Koa router params ke liye key mein ctx chahiye -- CacheKeyFn sirf req leta hai
common_mistakes: ctx.body = value (string value text/plain ban jaayega, null 204)
Client gone par bhi throw karna (error logs mein noise)
next() call karke downstream bhi chala dena
follow_up_questions: CacheKeyFn ko ctx kaise doge bina core badle?
Fastify adapter mein kya alag hoga?
Koa test mein disconnect case kaise likhoge?

question: Why is @CachedRoute a plain interceptor instance without dependency injection, and @Cached a legacy decorator, instead of a DI-based Nest cache module?
answer_hinglish:
PLAN ka decision: "@Cached is a framework-free legacy method decorator (works in NestJS and plain classes); the Nest route helper is an interceptor INSTANCE (no DI), like ratelimit-kit's guard."

Interceptor instance kyun: `UseInterceptors(new CachedRouteInterceptor(cache, options))` -- cache aur options decorator ko seedhe diye jaate hain. Na module registration, na provider token, na `@Inject`. Har route apna cache aur key le sakta hai. Cache ek module-level singleton hota hai (README: "One cache per KIND of data, created once"). Cost: interceptor DI container ke bahar hai, toh Nest ke providers (jaise ConfigService se TTL) inject nahi ho sakte, aur test mein cache swap karna module-level variable se hota hai, DI override se nahi.

Legacy decorator kyun: NestJS khud `experimentalDecorators` wale legacy decorators use karta hai; same kind likhne se `@Cached` Nest services mein bhi chalta hai aur plain classes / workers / scripts mein bhi, aur `cached.ts` Nest import nahi karta. TC39 standard decorators ka signature alag hai -- yeh NOT implemented.

Nest ka apna cache module bhi hota hai (`@nestjs/cache-manager` -- general knowledge, is repo mein use nahi). Jahan tak mujhe pata hai, uska interceptor default mein request URL se key banata hai -- jo per-user data ke liye wahi risk hai jiske against yahan key required hai. Yahan ke helpers single flight, abort, stale-while-revalidate aur TwoLevelCache ke saath tied hain -- woh features yahan ke core se aate hain.
why_needed: Framework integration mein DI vs plain objects ka trade-off har team face karti hai. Interviewer justification sunna chahta hai, sirf 'maine aise kiya' nahi.
real_world_analogy: Ghar mein apna water purifier (instance, seedha lagao) vs building ka central supply (DI module): apna lagana fast aur flexible, central supply ka config aur maintenance ek jagah.
how_it_works: Nest interceptors do tarah se: class (`UseInterceptors(MyInterceptor)`) -- Nest DI se banata hai; ya instance (`new MyInterceptor(...)`) -- Nest use as-is chalata hai, DI nahi. Legacy decorator = `(target, key, descriptor)`; standard decorator = `(value, context)`.
in_this_project: `src/adapters/nestjs.ts::CachedRoute` -> `applyDecorators(UseInterceptors(new CachedRouteInterceptor(cache, options)))`. `src/cached.ts` header comment: "Framework-free (a plain TypeScript legacy method decorator, the kind NestJS uses -- needs experimentalDecorators)". Test `test/nestjs-helper.test.ts` module-level `routeCache` aur `serviceCache`; `ProductService` bina DI ke `new` hota hai.
advantages: Zero setup, explicit dependencies
Same @Cached Nest aur non-Nest code mein
Har route apna cache/key
disadvantages: Nest providers inject nahi ho sakte
Test mein cache swap DI se nahi
Legacy decorators -- future TC39 migration
common_mistakes: Interceptor class pass karna aur constructor args expect karna (DI unhe nahi dega)
Cache ko request scope mein banana (har request naya cache)
Standard decorators ke saath experimentalDecorators mix karna
follow_up_questions: ConfigService se TTL chahiye toh kya karoge?
Interceptor ko DI-friendly kaise banaoge bina features khoye?
TC39 decorators par migrate karne mein kya badlega?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Simplicity aur portability (instance, legacy decorator, no framework import in core) vs Nest-native ergonomics (DI, config, testing overrides). Is project ne portability chuni kyunki same library workers aur scripts mein bhi chalni hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Cache ko galti se request-scoped bana diya (handler ke andar `new LruCache`) toh caching kabhi nahi hogi. Do modules alag-alag cache instances banaayein same data ke liye -- double memory, inconsistent invalidation.
advanced.alternatives: DI provider jo cache expose kare aur ek interceptor class jo `@Inject(CACHE)` le plus route metadata (`SetMetadata`) se key options; Nest ka built-in cache module; ya service layer mein explicit `getOrLoad` (sabse kam magic).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Bahut routes par per-route caches ka sprawl -- har ek ka apna maxEntries; total memory ka hisaab mushkil. 10x routes par ek central registry (DI) ka fayda badhta hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Ek optional DI wrapper module jo isi interceptor ko provider se cache de; caches ka registry jisse metrics ek endpoint par aayein; standard decorators ka variant.

question: Mutation testing took real effort in this project. What did it find that line coverage would not have, and is it worth the cost?
answer_hinglish:
Method pehle: ek deliberate bug `src/` mein, akela apply, poora suite chalao (`npx vitest run --reporter=json`, uppercase `H:` drive se, kyunki lowercase path par projects/18 mein vitest ne modules do baar load kiye), file byte-exact restore (checked). Har pattern pehle check hota hai ki exactly ek baar match kare. Runner repo ke bahar. Number = kitne tests fail hue. Stage 1: 42 breaks; stage 2: total 99 (42 re-based + 57 naye); stage 3: 20 framework-helper breaks -- kul 119 distinct breaks.

Kya mila jo coverage nahi deta (coverage sirf batata hai line chali; mutation batata hai ki line galat hone par koi test fail hota hai): (1) W5 ne test run HANG kiya -- weight loop forever; isse `size > 1` guard aur integer-only weights (W7) aaye, aur runner ab poora process tree kill karta hai. (2) L8 -- slow eviction wapas lana 0 tests fail -- naya call-count test. (3) Stage 2 ke 4 first-run survivors real test gaps the: X15 (test ne Redis timeout se pehle hi check kar liya), X16 (bad codec `undefined` deta tha jo doosra guard bhi pakadta), X24 (fake Redis synchronous, koi pending write nahi), X25 (PTTL exactly 0 kabhi produce nahi hua). (4) Stage 3: C4, E1, E2 -- real socket par invisible, fake response tests aaye; aur C7, D5, D6 un teen bugs ko guard karte hain jo interview bank ke review mein mile (stale serve 'miss' label, `@Cached` key ko `this` na milna, sync throw). Aur 3 equivalent mutants (L6, L7, W8) explain karke documented.

Worth it? Library code ke liye -- jahan concurrency, versions aur edge boundaries hain -- haan. Cost: har break ek full suite run, aur list haath se likhi hai (koi Stryker jaisa tool nahi), toh sirf woh bugs test hote hain jo author ne soche. README "caught by exactly one test" bhi list karta hai -- woh tests delete karna in bugs ko chhupa dega, yeh fragility ka map hai. Har app feature par main itna nahi karunga; core infra libraries par haan.
why_needed: Test quality ka sawal senior interviews mein aata hai: '100 percent coverage hai' kaafi nahi. Mutation testing test suite ko test karta hai.
real_world_analogy: Fire drill: building mein jaan-boojhkar ek alarm band karo aur dekho kaun notice karta hai. Agar koi nahi karta, toh tumhara monitoring andha hai -- chahe har room mein sensor (coverage) ho.
how_it_works: Mutant = code mein ek chhota deliberate change. Killed = koi test fail hua. Survived = ya toh test gap, ya equivalent mutant (behaviour same). Mutation score = killed / non-equivalent. Hand-picked mutants targeted hain; tools (Stryker) automatic par noisy.
in_this_project: README ke teen 'Mutation checks' sections (stage 1, 2, 3) har break ka naam aur failed count dete hain. Stage 3 ne core files (`cache.ts`, `two-level.ts`, `events.ts`) nahi badle, isliye 99 stage 1+2 breaks re-run nahi hue.
advantages: Test gaps concrete milte hain
Defensive design improvements (hang guard)
Har survivor explained -- trust badhta hai
disadvantages: Mehnga: har break = full suite
Hand-written list -- unsoche bugs miss
Process discipline chahiye (restore, timeouts, orphan processes)
common_mistakes: Coverage percentage ko test quality samajhna
Survivor ko bina analysis 'equivalent' bolna
Runner mein timeout ke saath child processes kill na karna
follow_up_questions: Stryker jaisa tool vs hand-picked mutants?
Mutation testing CI mein kaise fit karoge?
Equivalent mutants ko kaise identify karoge efficiently?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Hand-picked mutants: high signal, low noise, par author ki imagination tak limited. Automatic tools: broad par hazaron mutants, slow, aur bahut saare trivial/equivalent. Yahan targeted list chuni kyunki rules (TTL boundary, versions, NX) clear the.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Runner bug ne file restore na ki toh repo mein bug reh jaata -- isliye byte-exact check. W5 jaise hang ne orphan processes chhode jo baaki checks slow karte rahe. Ek test jo "exactly one" bugs pakadta hai, delete ho toh silent regression.
advanced.alternatives: Stryker (JS/TS ke liye mutation tool -- general knowledge, yahan use nahi); property-based testing (yahan model test already); fault injection in integration tests.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x code par full-suite-per-mutant ka cost bahut badhta hai -- incremental mutation (sirf changed files), test selection, parallel runners. 100x par sirf critical modules.
advanced.production_improvements: Runner ko repo mein (ya shared tooling mein) rakhna taaki reproducible ho; CI mein weekly run; "caught by exactly one test" list ko coverage report ke saath track karna.

question: Two Express instances share a TwoLevelCache over one Redis. Walk through a request on each instance and what X-Cache says.
answer_hinglish:
Test setup (`test/express-helper.test.ts`, real Redis, warna skip notice): har instance ka apna `TwoLevelCache` -- apna L1 (`LruCache`, maxEntries 100, ttlMs 60 000), `ioredisL2Client` ek connection par, `ioredisSubscriber` doosre connection par, dono ka same unique `prefix`. Dono par `cachedJson(cache, { key: () => "shared" }, producer)`.

Instance A request: `loadForRequest` -> `TwoLevelCache.getOrLoad` -> L1 miss -> L1 ka loader `loadThrough` -> `readL2` (GET + PTTL ek MULTI mein) -> Redis miss -> user loader (yahan `ran = true`) -> producer `{ from: "a" }`. Value L1 mein store aur `writeBehind`: `SET prefix+key value PX 60000 NX` background mein, await nahi -- response turant: `X-Cache: miss`. Isliye test Redis mein `EXISTS` poll karta hai jab tak key na aaye.

Instance B request: L1 miss -> `loadThrough` -> Redis HIT -> `context.ttlMs = min(PTTL, call TTL)` taaki B ki copy Redis copy se zyada na jiye -> value return; user loader kabhi nahi chala, `ran` false -> `X-Cache: hit`, body `{ from: "a" }`. `calls` = `{ a: 1, b: 0 }`.

System view: L1 per replica (fast, inconsistent window), Redis shared (ek DB load sab replicas ke liye). Invalidation: app update ke baad `cache.delete(key)` -- tombstone + publish, doosre replicas ka L1 drop. Redis down -> har call `l2TimeoutMs` (250 ms default) se bounded, read miss ban jaata hai, response phir bhi aata hai (X-Cache miss). Remaining windows README "Known" mein: silently cut subscriber L1 TTL tak purana serve karega, isliye L1 TTL chhota rakho.
why_needed: Multi-replica caching ka asli sawaal yahi hai: ek replica ka load doosre ke kaam aaye, aur update sab tak pahunche.
real_world_analogy: Do branch offices ek shared central record room (Redis) use karte hain, aur har office ki desk par photocopies (L1). Ek office ne file nikalwayi toh central room mein copy rakh di; doosra office central se le leta hai, archive (DB) tak nahi jaata.
how_it_works: Two-level cache: L1 in-process (nanoseconds-microseconds), L2 network cache (round trip), source of truth (DB). Read-through: L1 -> L2 -> DB. Write-behind to L2 after load. Pub/sub invalidation for L1 copies. SET NX + tombstones stale writes ko rokte hain.
in_this_project: `src/two-level.ts`: `getOrLoad` L1 load ke andar `loadThrough`; `readL2`; `writeBehind` (`pending` set, `flush()`); `set`/`delete` publish. `test/express-helper.test.ts` describe "two Express instances sharing a TwoLevelCache over one Redis"; cleanup mein `keys(prefix*)` delete aur connections quit.
advantages: Ek DB load sab replicas ke kaam
Redis outage par bhi reads chalte hain
Late stale writes NX/tombstone se refuse
disadvantages: Write-behind: response ke turant baad doosra replica Redis miss dekh sakta hai
Pub/sub fire-and-forget -- missed messages
Redis round trip cost naapa nahi
common_mistakes: Redis write ko await karke har miss slow karna
Subscriber ke liye same connection use karna (subscriber mode)
L1 TTL lamba rakhna jab replicas data share karein
follow_up_questions: Write-behind ki jagah write-through kab chahiye?
Dono replicas ek saath cold miss karein toh kya hota hai?
Cross-replica clear kaise banaoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Write-behind response latency bachata hai par ek chhota window chhodta hai jahan doosra replica Redis miss dekhe aur khud load kare. L1 copy ka TTL Redis PTTL se cap -- consistency ke liye, thodi zyada Redis reads ke cost par. Redis TTL sirf fresh part; stale grace per replica.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Redis down: L1 + loader, `set`/`delete` false resolve. Subscriber silently cut: purana L1 TTL tak. Load `tombstoneMs` se zyada slow: purani value wapas likh sakta hai -- tombstoneMs loader timeout se upar rakho. Race test: 20 rounds, recorded runs mein NX refusal 6, 14, 17, 11 rounds mein hit hua, Redis ne hamesha A ki value rakhi.
advanced.alternatives: Redis Streams (durable invalidation log), RESP3 client tracking (server-pushed invalidation) -- dono NOT implemented; Redis Cluster/Sentinel specifics bhi nahi; ya L1 hatakar sirf Redis (simple consistency, har read par network).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x replicas: har update ka publish sab tak -- pub/sub fan-out badhta hai; Redis ek shared bottleneck aur SPOF; L1 hit ratio replicas ke beech bant jaata hai. 100x: Redis Cluster, key hashing, aur shayad invalidation ke liye durable stream.
advanced.production_improvements: Redis round trip aur L2 hit latency benchmark; `stats()` (l2Hits, l2Errors, l2WritesSkipped, resubscribes) ko metrics mein; cross-replica clear (SCAN ya versioned prefix); Cluster support.

question: How are the stage-3 helpers layered so that the core library stays framework-free?
answer_hinglish:
Layers, neeche se upar. (1) Core: `src/cache.ts` (`LruCache`), `src/two-level.ts` (`TwoLevelCache`), `src/events.ts` -- koi framework nahi, koi runtime dependency nahi. Stage 3 ne inme se kuch nahi badla, isliye stage 1+2 ke 99 mutation breaks dobara nahi chalaye gaye. (2) `src/cached.ts` -- `@Cached`, framework-free legacy method decorator, sirf `Loadable` aur `SetOptions` types import karta hai. (3) `src/adapters/http.ts` -- shared HTTP core: `Loadable<V>` (structural interface: `getOrLoad(key, loader, options)` -- `LruCache<string, V>` aur `TwoLevelCache<V>` dono fit), `CacheKeyFn`, `CachedResponseOptions`, `requestSignal`, `loadForRequest`, `isNotFound`, `NOT_FOUND_BODY`. Sirf `node:http` types. (4) Framework edges: `src/adapters/express.ts` (`cachedJson`, Express runtime import nahi -- 4 aur 5 dono ke liye likha, 4.21.2 tested) aur `src/adapters/nestjs.ts` (`@nestjs/common` + `rxjs` import karta hai).

Packaging: `package.json` exports teen entry points -- `"."` -> `dist/index.js`, `"./express"`, `"./nestjs"`. `src/index.ts` core aur `Cached` export karta hai, aur HTTP types sirf `type` exports -- comment: "Framework helpers are separate entry points". `@nestjs/common` aur rxjs optional peer dependencies hain, toh jo sirf core ya Express use kare usse Nest install nahi karna padta.

Fayda: naya framework (Koa, Fastify) = ek patli file, core untouched. Structural interface ka matlab koi base class ya registration nahi.
why_needed: Library design interviews mein 'core ko framework se kaise alag rakhoge' common hai -- dependency direction aur packaging dono.
real_world_analogy: Mobile charger: ek hi adapter (core) aur alag-alag plugs (Express, Nest) -- naye desh ke liye sirf plug badlo.
how_it_works: Hexagonal / ports-and-adapters: core business logic ek interface (port) expose karta hai, adapters bahar ki duniya se jodte hain. Dependency hamesha andar ki taraf. Node package `exports` map alag entry points deta hai taaki optional deps sirf us entry point ke users ko chahiye hon.
in_this_project: `src/adapters/http.ts::Loadable` (comment: "LruCache<string, V> and TwoLevelCache<V> both fit (structural)"); `src/index.ts` last lines; `package.json` `exports`. README Files table har file ka role batata hai.
advantages: Core par framework ka koi asar nahi
Optional peer deps -- sirf jo chahiye woh install
Structural typing se L1 aur L2 dono plug
disadvantages: Teen entry points -- docs aur versioning zyada
Express helper Express types nahi deta, `req as express.Request` cast karna padta hai
Har adapter ke tests alag
common_mistakes: Core mein framework import kar dena
Nest ko hard dependency banana
Adapter mein business logic duplicate karna (http.ts ki jagah)
follow_up_questions: Fastify adapter ke liye kya chahiye?
Structural vs nominal interface ka trade-off?
Express 5 support kaise verify karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Separate entry points clean dependencies dete hain par API surface aur docs badhate hain. Node http types par Express helper likhna Express-version-agnostic hai, par developer ko `req` cast karna padta hai (tests mein `(req as express.Request).params`).
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar koi core file adapter ke liye badle (jaise LoadContext mein HTTP field), framework-free promise toot jaata. Optional peer dep missing ho aur koi `cache-kit/nestjs` import kare -- runtime import error.
advanced.alternatives: Ek monolithic package jo sab import kare (simple, heavy); alag npm packages per framework (cleanest, zyada release overhead); plugin registration system (overkill yahan).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada frameworks par yeh layering scale karti hai -- har naya adapter ek file. 10x users par semver aur entry-point-wise changelogs zaroori; abhi package npm par published hi nahi hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Express helper ke liye generic Req type ka better inference; Fastify aur Express 5 tests; package npm par publish karne se pehle exports ka type check (`types` conditions) -- abhi README kehta hai not published.
